text:
Mia Chen: Hey team — quick brain dump: we're splitting the client dependency graph between platform-owned pieces (routing/policy/telemetry contracts) and SDK-owned pieces (language bindings, helpers). Wanted to surface implementation options and risks before we lock anything.

Sanjay Patel: +1 we need to be explicit: platform should own canonical header names, quota attribution IDs, and route-policy semantics. SDKs own serialization, retries, and convenience helpers.

Emily R.: Is the plan to keep a tiny runtime shim in each SDK that translates SDK calls to platform headers? Concern: that shim ends up diverging and becomes a maintenance burden.

Kevin L: I'd rather we centralize the canonical mapping in a single npm/pypi/go module (very small) that all SDKs import. That avoids per-SDK duplication. Upside: one place for header normalization and sampling constants. Downside: publishing cadence and cross-language sync.

Mia Chen: Kevin — that aligns with one option we sketched. Two models: (A) single "redwood-client-contracts" multi-lang package (tiny, consumed by SDKs), or (B) platform publishes an HTTP negotiation endpoint + spec and SDKs implement it themselves. (B) means more work in SDKs, (A) centralizes risk. Thoughts?

Sanjay Patel: (B) has operational complexity for the platform (versioning, discovery). (A) is safer if we keep the contract stable and do semantic versioning. We should define a compatibility policy: patch = safe, minor = additive, major = breaking. Also add a feature flag for SDKs to opt into new headers at runtime for canaries.

Emily R.: If we go (A), team needs to agree on how the package exposes enums/constants. For Python: prefer simple constants dict + small helper functions. For TS: typed enums. For Go: const block + helper package. Keep surface minimal to avoid churn.

Devex Alice: UX note: console rollout will need a mapping table from route-policy id -> human label and default quota buckets. If the client contracts module introduces new IDs, we must ensure console can map unknown IDs gracefully (show numeric id + tooltip).

Kevin L: Implementation detail: propose we publish the contracts module from the infra repo using CI that cross-builds for each language. Example layout: \n\n```\ncontracts/\n  CHANGELOG.md\n  python/ (package: redwood_contracts)\n  ts/ (package: @redwood/contracts)\n  go/ (module: github.com/redwood/contracts)\n  spec.yaml\n```\n\nThis keeps source-of-truth in one place. SDKs add a dev-dependency and import.

Mia Chen: How do we handle hotfixes? If platform needs to add a telemetry sampling header immediately, we need SDKs to land and ship quickly. Can we support a shim fallback that recognizes unknown headers returned by platform?

Sanjay Patel: Yes: SDKs should accept and forward unknown headers (pass-through) and platform should send a "compatibility: v1" header when it adds new, non-breaking keys. For urgent changes we can ship a tiny runtime patch to the shared contracts package and bump patch versions.

Emily R.: Concern about Go module consumers: vendoring and slow update cadence. Suggest we add a long-lived opt-in flag in Redwood Console for "accept new header schema automatically" so older SDKs still work while customers opt-in.

Devex Alice: From rollout POV: we want a three-stage plan: feature flag in platform -> opt-in in Console per-tenant -> SDK package update and canary across clients. Add telemetry events: "contracts.updated", "sdk.consumed_contract_v" so we can track adoption.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment for contracts-service scheduled at 2026-03-23T15:00Z (id: canary-7182).

Kevin L: Telemetry naming: we need to converge on metric names for quota attributions. Propose: `redwood.quota.requested_tokens` and `redwood.quota.attributed_tenant`. Keep tag `route_policy_id`. If we publish those as constants in the contracts package, dashboards can import the names verbatim.

Mia Chen: One more compatibility risk: SDKs sometimes hide retry semantics. If platform changes route fallback order (cost vs latency preference), apps might observe different behavior even if headers unchanged. We should document that routing policy changes are considered behavior changes and tied to a major version bump of the contracts module.

Sanjay Patel: Agreed. Also: add an integration test harness in the contracts repo that exercises header normalization across SDK builds so we catch language-specific regressions early. Could be GH actions matrix.

Emily R.: TL;DR proposed action items: \n- pick model (A) single contracts repo (consensus here?)\n- Mia/Sanjay to draft compatibility policy doc and release cadence\n- Kevin to prototype CI cross-build for python/ts/go + example import in python-sdk and ts-sdk\n- Devex Alice to sketch console mapping fallback UI and telemetry events\n- Emily to own integration test matrix\n\nKevin L: I'm +1. I'll open a PR in infra/contracts with a minimal spec + the initial enums (route_policy, quota_bucket, metric names).

Mia Chen: Great — can we aim to land a design doc by EOD Friday and prototype CI next week? I can host a 30m sync Monday for owners. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
